title: How Adam Robinson scaled Get Emails/Retention.com to $13M ARR in 36 months with manual ABM
summary: Adam breaks down the lean outbound machine behind $13M ARR with six employees: a $3k/month Philippines team manually building target lists, a four-email sequence, a three-step LinkedIn flow, and ads to the same list. He also says what he would change today (multiple domains, sequencers, LinkedIn content) and why the 2020-21 conditions mattered.

principles.text: Build lists manually instead of pulling from Apollo/ZoomInfo; shared databases get hammered and reply rates collapse.
principles.quote: everyone else is using those same databases with those same emails. The problem is with the database platforms. Those email addresses get absolutely smashed.

principles.text: Target companies via technographics, then multi-thread 3-5 relevant people per account, always including the CEO.
principles.quote: We identified three to five potentially relevant people at each company.

principles.text: Cheap offshore labor works when you give them repeatable activity, not decisions or problems to solve.
principles.quote: We loaded them up with activity, not problems to solve.

principles.text: Run email, LinkedIn and ads against the same list so prospects feel you are everywhere.
principles.quote: combined with email LinkedIn, it created the impression that we were absolutely everywhere.

principles.text: High-volume outbound only accelerates a business that already has product-market fit; it cannot save one without word of mouth.
principles.quote: If you don't have word of mouth, which is the equivalent of product market fit, this will not save you.

principles.text: Today: still build lists manually, but send from separate domains, use a sequencer, and build organic LinkedIn content.
principles.quote: I'd set up multiple sending domains to protect the main brand domain.
